title: Trade
description: Selling a controlled substance on the street (D78, D82): whom you buy from and at what weights and prices, what a sale is, when buyers come to the corner, who sees, the heat it draws, and what holding and selling are charged as. The figures trace to CALIBRATION.md.

names.description: Whom the supplier is drawn from.

supplier.description: When the supplier can be found, and what they sell: a weight in tenths of a gram for a price in cents.

sale.description: What one buyer takes, in tenths of a gram, and pays, in cents.

corner.description: The corner where buyers come: in each hour of the day, the odds in percent that a buyer comes in each ten minutes; and of the town's people out on the street that hour, how many in a thousand pass the corner.

seen.description: The odds in percent a sale is seen and told of: a base, more for each person passing, in tenths of a percent, and more for heat, one percent for so many points; never above the most (tune).

heat.description: The police's attention to the corner and to you: points for a sale and for one seen, and what is kept of them each day, in ten-thousandths (tune).

possession.description: What holding it is charged as: the first whose weight covers what you hold, and your record.

delivery.description: What selling it, or holding it to sell, is charged as: the first whose weight covers it, and your record.

police.description: When the police act on what was seen (D46: at a time you are told): how many sales seen make a case, and days until they come for you.

bail.description: Bail at arraignment: the bond in cents, the share of it in percent you post to go home (MCL 765.6), and the hour of the morning the court sees the night's arrests.

court.description: Days from the arrest to the court date.

contest.description: The odds in percent a not-guilty plea ends in dismissal, by the evidence: sales seen only, or the drugs found on you.

crew.description: The supplier's crew (D79, D84–D86): the trust and the heat they want before they bring you in; what they front, at what price, due in how many days; trust lost when a front goes unpaid; and a recruit's terms (tune).

trust.description: Purchases or repayments before they'll bring you in.

heat.description: The most heat on you they'll take.

unpaid.description: Trust lost for a front not paid back on time.

regard.description: The coworker's regard needed for a yes.

familiarity.description: How well you must know them.

buyers.description: The odds in percent of a buyer in each of their ten minutes, through a night's four hours.

share.description: Percent of their takings they keep.

seen.description: The odds in percent one of their sales is seen.

named.description: The odds in percent they name you once arrested, at a regard of 0; less, a point for each point of regard.
